subject.title: [BUG]: Browser tool: `snapshot` returns page content before scroll, ignoring viewport position

question: Should browser `snapshot` become a visible-viewport read after scroll, or should OpenClaw add a separate visible-viewport read while keeping `snapshot` as the full UI-tree/read surface?
rationale: The current implementation is internally consistent as a tree snapshot, but the user problem is real for agents that need to verify below-the-fold state; changing default snapshot semantics affects model-facing browser contracts and compatibility across Playwright, raw CDP, and Chrome MCP.

options.title: Add visible-viewport read
options.body: Add an explicit viewport-scoped read with scroll metadata and keep existing full AI/ARIA/tree snapshots as an escape hatch.

options.title: Change snapshot default
options.body: Make `snapshot` itself viewport-scoped after scroll and require callers to opt into full-tree reads when they need them.

options.title: Keep tree snapshots
options.body: Document that `snapshot` is a full UI-tree read and direct agents to screenshots or labeled screenshots for visible viewport checks.

recommendation.title: Add visible-viewport read
recommendation.body: Add an explicit viewport-scoped read with scroll metadata and keep existing full AI/ARIA/tree snapshots as an escape hatch.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the browser plugin product contract and compatibility boundary, which traces most strongly to the bundled browser runtime ownership move and docs/product surface history.
